subject: Audit-log preservation & transfer process — questions and SOP draft
messages:
From: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@globex.com>

Date: 2027-05-12 16:14:00 -0700
Subject: RFP Q: log preservation, export and handoff options

Markus —

Thanks for the product brief earlier today. Security has a few targeted questions for our procurement RFP about audit-log preservation and exportability. We need clear, machine-checkable answers for each item below so we can include them in the SOX/ITGC appendix. Can you confirm and provide any SOPs or templates you already use?

1) Retention windows by data type (auth events, admin config changes, request traces, model-inference metadata) — can these be set per-tenant?
2) Are logs stored immutably (WORM) once finalized? If yes, what mechanism (object lock, append-only ledger)?
3) Export formats and tooling — preferred formats, max export size, streaming export vs snapshot, and checksums provided?
4) Transfer process for large evidence packages — SFTP, presigned S3, vendor-managed transfer? How do you ensure integrity and chain-of-custody?
5) Time zone and timestamp provenance — UTC only? signed timestamps?
6) RPO/RTO for audit-log retrieval in incident/legal requests — typical SLA windows for ad-hoc extracts?

We're on a tight timeline; security would like answers plus any templates by EOD Friday (2027-05-14).

Thanks,
Priya Sharma
Senior IT Risk Manager
Globex Corporation

Subject: Re: RFP Q: log preservation, export and handoff options

Priya —

Thanks for the clear list. I'm attaching a short matrix and will loop in Laura and Mina for the SOP detail. High-level answers up front to keep you moving:

1) Retention windows: yes — per-tenant configurable retention for the following classes: auth events (default 365d), admin config changes (default 7y), request traces (default 90d), model-inference metadata (default 180d). We support shorter/longer for enterprise contracts; we can map these to your regulatory buckets.

2) Immutability: we provide an optional WORM mode backed by object-lock on S3-compatible storage for Hosted and Dedicated. For Private deployments we provide configuration guidance and an HLD for append-only journaling.

3) Exports: exports support NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON) and Parquet. We offer streaming exports via paginated APIs for live pulls and snapshot exports for point-in-time packaging. Each export includes SHA256 checksums and a manifest.json. Max single-snapshot size: 10TB; larger packages are sharded with a manifest and per-chunk checksums.

4) Transfer: standard is presigned S3 URLs (timeboxed) or customer SFTP endpoints. For especially large legal holds we can provision a temporary, encrypted transfer bucket and provide an HMAC-signed manifest plus a chain-of-custody PDF generated at handoff.

5) Timestamps: we store and surface all logs in UTC. All internal service timestamps are monotonic wall-clock + monotonic counter for ordering; exports include original event timestamp and server-received timestamp. When requested we can provide GPG-signed manifest timestamps for legal packages.

6) Retrieval SLA: ad-hoc small exports (<100GB): best-effort within 4 hours; medium packages (100GB–2TB): 24–48 hours; large packages (>2TB): we agree a window during the intake (typically 3–7 business days) and provide a transfer plan. Enterprise contract customers can include a guaranteed evidence delivery SLA.

I'll attach the draft matrix and chain-of-custody template. Laura, Mina — can you prepare an SOP outline (requested by Friday EOD) that covers: intake form, verification steps, manifest generation, transfer modes, and custody acknowledgment?

Best,
Markus Klein
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: RFP Q: log preservation & transfer — SOP outline

Priya —

Following Markus' summary, attached is an SOP outline and a short FAQ to help your auditors validate our controls. Key operational details (expanded):

- Intake & Authorization: requests hit our Evidence Intake form (we'll send a secure link). Each request must include requestor name, legal basis, scope (tenant IDs, date range), required formats, and destination endpoint. Intake generates a UUID and a chain-of-custody PDF stub.

- Data Assembly: we produce a point-in-time snapshot using a consistent snapshot vector (ledger sequence + UTC timestamp) to guarantee no partial windows. For streaming exports, we provide sequence tokens to resume.

- Packaging: snapshot archives are created as compressed shards (Parquet or NDJSON), each with a per-file SHA256 and a signed manifest.json. Manifests include: snapshot vector, shard list, per-shard checksum, total byte count, and a signed timestamp.

- Transfer modes supported: presigned S3 (default), customer SFTP, or secure courier for on-prem physical handoff for very large drives (rare). Each transfer includes signed manifests.

- Chain-of-custody: upon transfer initiation we generate a custody PDF that lists custodians, timestamp, manifest hash, and signatures from the Redwood transfer operator. For legal holds we will notarize the custody PDF on request (additional service).

- Verification: recipient runs per-shard checksum validation against manifest; we also provide an expected file-tree layout and a simple verification script (Python) for convenience.

- Retention enforcement: deletion is by tenant policy; in WORM mode deletions require an admin legal-unlock with multi-party approval logged to the audit ledger.

I have attached an SOP skeletal doc (internal) and the chain-of-custody template. Mina — please draft the intake form and the verification script snippet and drop them in the Drive link Markus provided.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Director, Security & Compliance Ops
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: RFP Q: audit-log preservation & transfer — artifacts

Priya, team —

Attached are the artifacts we discussed: the preservation matrix (breaks down defaults and configurable ranges), the chain-of-custody template (fillable PDF), and an implementation note on presigned S3 transfer process including signed-manifest examples. Excerpt of the presigned process:

- Redwood generates N encrypted shards and uploads them to a temporary transfer bucket in the redwood-account. Each shard name follows: <tenant>-snapshot-<yyyyMMddTHHmmss>-shard-<n>.parquet
- We compute SHA256 for each shard and write manifest.json: {"snapshot_vector": "seq-12345@20270518T152200Z", "shards": [{"name": "...", "sha256": "..."}], "total_bytes": 123456789}
- Provide presigned GET URLs with 2-hour TTL to the recipient (or longer if negotiated) via encrypted email or secure portal.
- On handoff we record: custody operator, manifest hash, recipient identity, IP address of first GET, and timestamp.

Also attached a short sample output from our verification script that shows successful checksum validation and a signed manifest timestamp using our internal signing key (we can provide the public key for verification).

If you want, we can run a dry-run transfer to your SFTP endpoint next week; that usually helps the auditors validate the flow end-to-end.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Product Security Engineer
Redwood Inference
